name: Business Technology & Digital Literacy
description: Foundational digital literacy for the modern business world — productivity tools, spreadsheets, data basics, internet skills, cybersecurity awareness, and professional digital communication.

modules.title: Digital Literacy Foundations
modules.objectives: Identify hardware and software components; understand operating systems; manage files and folders; navigate the internet safely. Students will evaluate realistic scenarios, apply concepts to decisions, and justify recommendations with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: Practice naming, organizing, and locating files in a clear folder structure.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 1: Digital Literacy Foundations.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Draw and label your own desktop-computer system diagram with at least eight hardware components and one sentence describing each component function. Then create a three-level folder tree for a fictional school project and provide a text outline or screenshot containing no personal files. Evaluation: eight accurate labels, correct hardware functions, logical folder names, and a complete three-level structure. Submit the labeled diagram and folder-tree outline, and explain why two naming or organization choices would help a teammate find the correct file.

modules.title: Professional Email & Communication
modules.objectives: Write professional emails using correct tone, structure, and etiquette; use CC, BCC, and Reply-All appropriately; understand professional messaging norms. Students will evaluate realistic scenarios, apply concepts to decisions, and justify recommendations with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: Review subject lines, tone, structure, and recipient choices for professional email.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 2: Professional Email & Communication.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Draft three professional emails: a request for information, a post-interview follow-up, and an apology for a missed deadline. Annotate the subject line, greeting, purpose, requested action, closing, and any appropriate CC or BCC choice. Evaluation: clear subject lines, professional tone, concise action requests, correct recipient handling, and proofreading. Submit an annotated email portfolio and explain why each tone and recipient-field choice fits its audience.

modules.title: Word Processing & Document Design
modules.objectives: Use Google Docs or Microsoft Word to create, format, and style documents; apply headings, margins, spacing, and templates; produce a professional report.
modules.readingNote: Practice document structure, headings, formatting, and collaboration features.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 3: Word Processing & Document Design.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Create a two-page report about a technology topic using a title, Heading 1 and Heading 2 styles, body text, one bulleted list, one labeled table, page numbers, and at least two cited sources. Submit the document and a screenshot of its navigation outline. Evaluation: correct style hierarchy, consistent spacing and typography, readable table, accurate citations, and a working outline. Explain why the heading hierarchy and table design make the report easier to navigate and verify.

modules.title: Spreadsheets: Basics
modules.objectives: Enter and format data in Google Sheets or Excel; use basic formulas: SUM, AVERAGE, IF, COUNT; understand cell references. Students will analyze examples, explain the relevant concept in context, and create a short written or visual product that demonstrates mastery.
modules.readingNote: Apply spreadsheet formatting and basic formulas to a monthly budget.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 4: Spreadsheets: Basics.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Build a one-month fictional personal budget with at least two income rows and eight expense categories. Use SUM for totals, AVERAGE for average expense, COUNT for the number of recorded expenses, and IF to flag any category over its budget. Apply currency formatting and conditional highlighting. Evaluation: correct formulas, valid cell references, complete categories, readable formatting, and a 100-word interpretation of the result. Submit the workbook and the 100-word interpretation, citing at least three calculated values as evidence.

modules.title: Spreadsheets: Data Analysis
modules.objectives: Sort and filter data; use VLOOKUP; create pivot tables; build charts to visualize data trends. Students will evaluate realistic scenarios, apply concepts to decisions, and justify recommendations with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: Practice sorting, filtering, lookup formulas, pivot tables, and charts.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 5: Spreadsheets: Data Analysis.
modules.practiceNote: Download this deterministic 50-row CSV for the Module 5 sort, Q3 filter, VLOOKUP, pivot-table, and bar-chart assignment.
modules.assignment: Download the 50-row sales-records CSV linked in this module and import it into a spreadsheet. Sort Revenue from highest to lowest; filter Quarter to Q3; use the lookup table P101=Notebook, P102=Headset, P103=Webcam, P104=Desk Lamp, P105=Backpack, P106=Calculator to add ProductName with VLOOKUP; create a pivot table of Revenue by Category; and build a labeled bar chart. Evaluation: correct import, reproducible sort and filter, working VLOOKUP, accurate pivot totals, and a readable chart. Submit the completed spreadsheet and chart plus a short explanation of what the pivot result shows, citing two values from the data.

modules.title: Presentations & Slide Design
modules.titleZh: 演示文稿与幻灯片设计
modules.objectives: Build effective presentations in Google Slides or PowerPoint; apply design principles: visual hierarchy, color, font, and white space; structure a narrative with slides.
modules.readingNote: Review slide organization, visual hierarchy, readable text, and consistent design.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 6: Presentations & Slide Design.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Create a ten-slide presentation for a fictional business idea: title, agenda, six content slides, one evidence or data slide, and a closing call to action. Use one font family, a three-color palette, clear hierarchy, meaningful white space, and at least two cited data visuals. Evaluation: complete narrative, readable slides, consistent design, accurate labels and citations, and a specific closing action.

modules.title: Cloud Computing & Collaboration
modules.objectives: Use Google Drive or OneDrive to store, share, and collaborate on files; understand version history; apply real-time co-editing best practices. Students will evaluate realistic scenarios, apply concepts to decisions, and justify recommendations with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: Review Drive sharing roles and choose the least-permissive access that still supports collaboration.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 7: Cloud Computing & Collaboration.
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Create a fictional team-project folder with a document, spreadsheet, and presentation. Share each artifact using the least-permissive role needed for a teacher or class partner, add one comment and one suggestion, and identify one earlier version in version history. Submit a permission matrix and a 200-word reflection; do not expose personal account details. Evaluation: correct roles, evidence of collaboration features, accurate version-history explanation, and privacy-aware sharing.

modules.title: Internet Research & Information Literacy
modules.objectives: Evaluate sources for credibility and bias; use Boolean search operators; fact-check claims; identify misinformation. Students will evaluate realistic scenarios, apply concepts to decisions, and justify recommendations with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: Practice current Google Search operators for exact phrases, exclusions, domains, and related pages.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video for Module 8: Internet Research & Information Literacy.
modules.video2Note: TED-Ed — How to spot a misleading graph
modules.practiceNote: Apply the linked guidance to the module assignment and record the evidence or steps named in the task.
modules.assignment: Compare three reports about the same factual claim using SIFT. Record the exact search queries used, including one phrase search and one exclusion or site-limited search; investigate each publisher; trace the claim to original evidence; and rank the sources by reliability with a one-page justification. Evaluation: reproducible queries, all SIFT steps, primary-source tracing, citations, and evidence-based ranking.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of hardware?
questions.answer: A keyboard
questions.explanation: Hardware refers to the physical components of a computer. A keyboard is a physical input device.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct structure for a professional email?
options: Subject line, greeting, body, professional closing, signature
questions.answer: Subject line, greeting, body, professional closing, signature
questions.explanation: Professional emails follow the structure: clear subject line, polite greeting, organized body, professional closing (e.g., 'Best regards'), and a signature.

questions.question: In an email, BCC stands for:
questions.answer: Blind Carbon Copy
questions.explanation: BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) sends a copy of the email to additional recipients without other recipients seeing their addresses.

questions.question: Which Google Docs feature lets you preview and restore an earlier saved version of a document?
questions.answer: Version History
questions.explanation: Version History logs saved changes, identifies contributors, and lets an authorized user restore an earlier version.

questions.question: Which spreadsheet formula adds all numeric values in cells A1 through A10?
questions.answer: =SUM(A1:A10)
questions.explanation: SUM adds the numeric values in the specified range; COUNT would only count numeric cells.

questions.question: What does the AVERAGE function do in a spreadsheet?
options: Finds the largest value in a range
Counts the number of cells with data
Calculates the arithmetic mean of a range of numbers
Rounds all values to the nearest integer
questions.answer: Calculates the arithmetic mean of a range of numbers
questions.explanation: =AVERAGE(range) sums all values in the range and divides by the count of those values to return the arithmetic mean.

questions.question: Which design principle means that the most important element on a slide should visually stand out the most?
questions.answer: Visual hierarchy
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Visual hierarchy.

questions.question: Which option best defines cloud storage?
options: Files stored on remote servers and accessed through a network
Files stored only on a USB drive
Files available only on the device that created them
Files that never require account or access controls
questions.answer: Files stored on remote servers and accessed through a network
questions.explanation: Cloud storage keeps files on remote infrastructure so authorized users and devices can access them through a network.

questions.question: Using the Boolean search operator AND in a search engine:
options: Finds pages with either of the terms
Excludes a term from search results
Requires both terms to appear in results
questions.answer: Requires both terms to appear in results
questions.explanation: Boolean AND narrows a search by requiring all connected terms to be present in every result returned.

questions.question: Which characteristic is a red flag that an email might be a phishing attempt?
options: It comes from a known colleague
It asks you to verify your password by clicking a link
It has a formal greeting and signature
It was sent during business hours
questions.answer: It asks you to verify your password by clicking a link
questions.explanation: Legitimate organizations never ask for passwords via email. Urgent requests to click links and enter credentials are classic phishing tactics.

questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest password?
questions.answer: Tr#9kL!mQ2@v
questions.explanation: Strong passwords are long, use a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols, and avoid common words or personal information.

questions.question: Which option correctly defines a person’s digital footprint?
options: A printed record of computer purchases
The trail of data associated with online actions and interactions
A hardware component that stores files
A browser used only for private searches
questions.answer: The trail of data associated with online actions and interactions
questions.explanation: A digital footprint includes information intentionally shared and data recorded through online activity.

questions.question: When sharing a Google Drive file, setting access to 'Viewer' means the recipient can:
options: Only view the file without making changes
questions.answer: Only view the file without making changes
questions.explanation: Viewer access allows recipients to see the file contents but not edit, comment, or share it.

questions.question: You receive an email from 'support@paypa1.com' saying your account has been suspended and you must click a link immediately to restore access. Identify two specific red flags in this scenario and explain what you should do.
questions.answer: Red flags: (1) misspelled domain name (paypa1.com uses the number '1' instead of the letter 'l'); (2) urgency/pressure tactic ('immediately'). Action: do not click the link; go directly to the official website by typing the URL; report the email as phishing.
questions.explanation: Phishing emails commonly use lookalike domains and create urgency to trick users into acting before thinking critically.

questions.question: A classmate says, 'Cloud storage is risky — I only save files on my computer.' Provide two advantages of cloud storage over local storage only, and one valid concern your classmate might have.
questions.answer: Advantages: (1) files are accessible from any internet-connected device; (2) automatic backup prevents data loss if the device is lost or damaged. Valid concern: if the internet is unavailable or the cloud provider has an outage, files may be temporarily inaccessible; also, privacy concerns about data stored on third-party servers.
questions.explanation: Cloud storage offers significant convenience and redundancy, but relying solely on the cloud introduces internet dependency and third-party privacy risks.

questions.question: Which component is commonly described as the computer's processor because it executes instructions?
questions.answer: CPU
questions.explanation: The central processing unit executes program instructions and coordinates many computing operations.

questions.question: The subject line of a professional email should be:
options: Long and detailed to explain everything
Concise and descriptive of the email's purpose
Written in all capital letters to grab attention
questions.answer: Concise and descriptive of the email's purpose
questions.explanation: A good subject line is brief yet informative, giving the recipient a clear idea of the email's content before opening it.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word or Google Docs, 'Styles' are used to:
options: Apply consistent formatting to headings and body text throughout a document
Convert the document to a PDF
questions.answer: Apply consistent formatting to headings and body text throughout a document
questions.explanation: Styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, Normal, etc.) enforce consistent formatting and allow automatic generation of a table of contents.

questions.question: Which spreadsheet formula returns "Pass" when A1 is 60 or above and "Fail" otherwise?
questions.answer: =IF(A1>=60, "Pass", "Fail")
questions.explanation: IF tests the condition A1>=60 and returns "Pass" when true and "Fail" when false.

questions.question: What is VLOOKUP primarily used to do in a spreadsheet?
options: Find a value in the first column of a table and return a related value from the same row
Count every nonblank cell in a worksheet
Combine multiple files into one workbook
Apply conditional formatting to a chart
questions.answer: Find a value in the first column of a table and return a related value from the same row
questions.explanation: VLOOKUP matches a lookup value in the table’s first column and retrieves a value from another column in that row.

questions.question: Which chart type is best for showing how a whole is divided into parts (e.g., budget by category)?
questions.answer: Pie chart
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Pie chart.

questions.question: What does the '6 × 6 rule' for presentations suggest?
options: Use at least 6 fonts per slide
Use no more than 6 bullet points per slide and 6 words per bullet
Have at least 6 slides with 6 paragraphs each
questions.answer: Use no more than 6 bullet points per slide and 6 words per bullet
questions.explanation: The 6×6 rule is a design guideline to keep slides uncluttered: max 6 bullet points per slide and 6 words per bullet.

questions.question: Real-time collaboration in Google Drive means:
options: Only one person can edit the document at a time
Multiple users can edit the same document simultaneously and see each other's changes live
The document is updated only when it is re-uploaded
Changes are saved only when the document is closed
questions.answer: Multiple users can edit the same document simultaneously and see each other's changes live
questions.explanation: Google Workspace tools support real-time collaboration, allowing multiple contributors to work simultaneously with live updates visible to all editors.

questions.question: What does SIFT stand for when evaluating online information?
options: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace claims to the original context
questions.answer: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace claims to the original context
questions.explanation: SIFT slows down an initial reaction, investigates the source, compares coverage, and traces evidence to its original context.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects an account in addition to a strong password?
options: Sharing the password with a trusted friend
Using the same password across all accounts
Writing the password on a sticky note
questions.answer: Enabling two-factor authentication (2FA)
questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication adds a second verification step (e.g., a code sent to your phone), making it significantly harder for attackers to access your account even if they know your password.

questions.question: Which sharing setting is appropriate for a reviewer who should comment on a cloud document but should not directly rewrite it?
questions.answer: Commenter
questions.explanation: Commenter access supports feedback while limiting direct changes to the document.

questions.question: A spreadsheet contains hundreds of sales rows. Which tool should be used to show only Q3 records without deleting the others?
questions.answer: Filter
questions.explanation: A filter temporarily hides rows that do not meet the selected condition while preserving the dataset.

questions.question: Which formula correctly counts numeric entries in cells B2 through B20?
questions.answer: =COUNT(B2:B20)
questions.explanation: COUNT returns the number of cells in the range that contain numeric values.

questions.question: Which chart is usually clearest for comparing total revenue across a small set of product categories?
questions.answer: Bar chart
questions.explanation: A labeled bar chart supports direct comparison of values across discrete categories.

questions.question: A team needs several people to edit the same proposal at the same time. Which feature directly supports this?
options: Printing one copy for each person
questions.answer: Real-time co-editing
questions.explanation: Real-time co-editing lets authorized collaborators work in the same cloud document and see changes as they occur.

questions.question: Which formula would count only the cells in B1:B20 that contain numerical values (not blank or text)?
questions.answer: =COUNT(B1:B20)
questions.explanation: =COUNT counts only cells containing numbers. =COUNTA counts all non-empty cells including text.

questions.question: What is a pivot table used to do?
options: Summarize and analyze records by selected categories or fields
Turn every cell into plain text
Replace source data with a screenshot
questions.answer: Summarize and analyze records by selected categories or fields
questions.explanation: A pivot table groups records and calculates summaries such as totals or averages without changing the source rows.

questions.question: Which search query is best for finding PDF reports about renewable energy only on a government domain?
questions.answer: site:.gov filetype:pdf "renewable energy"
questions.explanation: The domain, file-type, and exact-phrase operators narrow results to government PDF reports on the stated topic.

questions.question: You are asked to analyze sales data for a small business. Describe the steps you would take in a spreadsheet to (1) calculate total and average monthly sales, (2) identify the top 3 months by revenue, and (3) create a visual to present your findings.
questions.answer: (1) Use =SUM() for total sales and =AVERAGE() for average monthly sales. (2) Sort the revenue column in descending order or use LARGE() to find the top 3 values. (3) Select the monthly data and insert a bar or column chart, add a title and axis labels, to clearly visualize revenue trends.
questions.explanation: Effective data analysis in a spreadsheet combines formulas for calculation, sorting/filtering for ranking, and charts for visual communication.

questions.question: Describe two access or collaboration controls a team should use when sharing a cloud project and explain the risk each control reduces.
questions.answer: Use least-privilege sharing roles so viewers, commenters, and editors receive only the permissions they need; this reduces accidental or unauthorized changes. Limit link access to named people or the intended organization and review the access list; this reduces unintended disclosure. Version history and clear file naming can also support accountability and recovery.
questions.explanation: A strong response connects specific sharing or collaboration controls to the risks of unwanted edits, disclosure, or loss of earlier work.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is an example of software?
quizQuestions.answer: Google Chrome browser
quizQuestions.explanation: Software is a set of programs or instructions. Google Chrome is an application (software); the others are hardware.

quizQuestions.question: In computer memory terminology, what does the abbreviation RAM stand for?
quizQuestions.answer: Random Access Memory
quizQuestions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the computer's short-term memory that holds data currently in use by the processor.

quizQuestions.question: Which file-management choice makes a team project easiest to navigate?
options: Store every file on the desktop
Use descriptive file names and folders organized by project and content type
Keep duplicate copies in random folders
quizQuestions.answer: Use descriptive file names and folders organized by project and content type
quizQuestions.explanation: Clear names and a predictable folder hierarchy help collaborators locate the correct version.

quizQuestions.question: Short response: Which of the following is an input device?
quizQuestions.answer: Mouse
quizQuestions.explanation: A correct response identifies "Mouse" and connects it to the module context.

quizQuestions.question: Which greeting is most appropriate for a professional email to a potential employer?
quizQuestions.answer: Dear Mr. Kim,
quizQuestions.explanation: Professional emails use formal greetings. 'Dear [Title Last Name],' is the standard respectful opening.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the CC field in an email?
options: To send a copy to additional recipients who should be aware of the message
To attach files to the email
quizQuestions.answer: To send a copy to additional recipients who should be aware of the message
quizQuestions.explanation: CC (Carbon Copy) sends a visible copy to other recipients, signaling they are included for awareness but are not the primary audience.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is the best subject line for a professional email?
quizQuestions.answer: Meeting Request — Project Kickoff — April 30
quizQuestions.explanation: A good subject line is specific and informative, telling the recipient exactly what the email is about at a glance.

quizQuestions.question: When is BCC most appropriate in a professional email?
options: When all recipients should reply to one another
When sending to a large external list whose addresses should remain private
quizQuestions.answer: When sending to a large external list whose addresses should remain private
quizQuestions.explanation: BCC hides recipient addresses from the other recipients and can protect privacy on a large external mailing.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of using heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2) in a document?
options: To change the document's page orientation
To create consistent formatting and enable a navigable outline
To insert a table of images
quizQuestions.answer: To create consistent formatting and enable a navigable outline
quizQuestions.explanation: Heading styles apply consistent formatting and allow document navigation tools and automatic table of contents generation.

quizQuestions.question: Which keyboard shortcut is used to make selected text bold in most word processors?
quizQuestions.answer: Ctrl + B
quizQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + B (Cmd + B on Mac) applies bold formatting to selected text in Google Docs, Microsoft Word, and most word processors.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'margin' refer to in document design?
options: The font size used in the document
The blank space around the edges of a page
The number of words per line
The color of the page background
quizQuestions.answer: The blank space around the edges of a page
quizQuestions.explanation: Margins are the white space borders on all four sides of a page that frame the content and improve readability.

quizQuestions.question: Short response: Which line spacing setting provides the most white space between lines, improving readability for longer documents?
quizQuestions.answer: Double (2.0)
quizQuestions.explanation: A correct response identifies "Double (2.0)" and connects it to the module context.

quizQuestions.question: In a spreadsheet, a cell reference like 'B3' refers to:
quizQuestions.answer: Column B, Row 3
quizQuestions.explanation: Cell references use the column letter followed by the row number. B3 is the cell at Column B, Row 3.

quizQuestions.question: What does the =COUNT(A1:A10) formula do?
options: Adds all values in A1 to A10
Counts the number of cells in A1:A10 that contain numbers
Finds the largest value in A1:A10
quizQuestions.answer: Counts the number of cells in A1:A10 that contain numbers
quizQuestions.explanation: COUNT returns the number of cells in the selected range that contain numeric values; it does not add or average them.

quizQuestions.question: What is an absolute cell reference in a spreadsheet (e.g., $A$1)?
options: A cell reference that changes when you copy a formula to another cell
A cell reference that stays fixed regardless of where the formula is copied
A reference to a cell in another spreadsheet file
A cell that cannot be edited
quizQuestions.answer: A cell reference that stays fixed regardless of where the formula is copied
quizQuestions.explanation: Adding $ signs locks the column and/or row reference. $A$1 always points to cell A1 no matter where the formula is moved.

quizQuestions.question: The formula =IF(B2>100, "Over Budget", "OK") will display "Over Budget" when:
quizQuestions.answer: B2 is greater than 100
quizQuestions.explanation: IF evaluates whether B2 is greater than 100 and returns the first text value, "Over Budget," only when that condition is true.

quizQuestions.question: What does sorting data in a spreadsheet allow you to do?
options: Arrange data in ascending or descending order based on a column
Change the font of all cells
quizQuestions.answer: Arrange data in ascending or descending order based on a column
quizQuestions.explanation: Sorting reorders rows based on values in a selected column, either from A to Z (ascending) or Z to A (descending).

quizQuestions.question: What does a filter in a spreadsheet do?
options: Changes the color of cells based on value
Hides rows that do not meet specified criteria, making it easier to focus on relevant data
Removes all formulas from a range
Copies data to a new sheet
quizQuestions.answer: Hides rows that do not meet specified criteria, making it easier to focus on relevant data
quizQuestions.explanation: Filters temporarily hide rows that don't match your criteria, allowing you to view and analyze a subset of your data.

quizQuestions.question: In VLOOKUP, why is an exact-match setting useful for product IDs?
options: It returns the nearest alphabetical item
It requires the ID to match a lookup-table entry exactly
quizQuestions.answer: It requires the ID to match a lookup-table entry exactly
quizQuestions.explanation: Product IDs are discrete identifiers, so an exact match prevents a nearby but incorrect lookup result.

quizQuestions.question: Which tool best summarizes total revenue by product category without writing a separate formula for each category?
quizQuestions.answer: Pivot table
quizQuestions.explanation: A pivot table groups records by category and calculates summaries such as total revenue.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is a best practice for slide text?
options: Include complete paragraphs so the audience can read everything
Use bullet points with brief phrases, not full sentences
Use 3 different fonts per slide for variety
Avoid using any text and rely only on images
quizQuestions.answer: Use bullet points with brief phrases, not full sentences
quizQuestions.explanation: Slides should support the speaker, not replace them. Brief bullet points keep slides clean and the audience focused on the presenter.

quizQuestions.question: A slide's color palette should ideally consist of:
options: As many colors as possible to look creative
A different color for every slide
quizQuestions.answer: 2–3 complementary colors used consistently
quizQuestions.explanation: A limited, consistent color palette creates visual cohesion and professionalism. Too many colors look chaotic and distract from the content.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a title slide in a presentation?
options: To list every topic that will be covered in detail
To introduce the topic, presenter, and context to the audience
To display the data and conclusions
To show the references and sources used
quizQuestions.answer: To introduce the topic, presenter, and context to the audience
quizQuestions.explanation: The title slide sets the stage — it shows the presentation topic, the presenter's name, and often the date or organization.

quizQuestions.question: What creates the clearest visual hierarchy on a presentation slide?
options: Making every element the same size
Using size, position, and contrast to emphasize the main message
quizQuestions.answer: Using size, position, and contrast to emphasize the main message
quizQuestions.explanation: Visual hierarchy directs attention by making the most important information visually prominent.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using cloud storage for team projects?
options: Only one person can work on a file at a time
Files can be accessed and edited from any device with internet access
Files are permanently deleted after 30 days
Cloud storage does not require an internet connection
quizQuestions.answer: Files can be accessed and edited from any device with internet access
quizQuestions.explanation: Cloud storage enables access from any internet-connected device, supporting remote collaboration and eliminating the need to email files back and forth.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'version history' allow you to do in Google Docs?
options: Delete all previous versions of a document
See who made changes and restore earlier versions of the document
Share the document with new users
Convert the document to a spreadsheet
quizQuestions.answer: See who made changes and restore earlier versions of the document
quizQuestions.explanation: Version history tracks every saved change, letting collaborators see who edited what and when, and restore earlier versions if needed.

quizQuestions.question: Which sharing permission is safest for someone who only needs to read a cloud document?
quizQuestions.answer: Viewer
quizQuestions.explanation: Viewer access follows least privilege by allowing reading without permission to change the file.

quizQuestions.question: Which Boolean search operator would you use to exclude a word from search results?
quizQuestions.answer: NOT
quizQuestions.explanation: The Boolean operator NOT (or a minus sign in Google) excludes terms from results. E.g., 'jaguar NOT car' returns results about the animal, not the vehicle.

quizQuestions.question: Which domain extension is most commonly associated with government websites in the United States?
quizQuestions.answer: .gov
quizQuestions.explanation: The .gov domain is restricted to U.S. government entities, making it a reliable indicator of official government information.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is the best indicator that a website is a reliable source?
options: It cites peer-reviewed studies and identifies its authors
It appears at the top of Google search results
It has been shared many times on social media
quizQuestions.answer: It cites peer-reviewed studies and identifies its authors
quizQuestions.explanation: Credible sources identify their authors, cite verifiable evidence, and have editorial oversight — not simply high traffic or eye-catching design.

quizQuestions.question: Which search query requires the words climate risk to appear together in that exact order?
quizQuestions.answer: "climate risk"
quizQuestions.explanation: Quotation marks keep the two words together as one exact search phrase instead of matching them separately anywhere on a page.
